title: Dissociation of Colorectal Biopsies
author: Alan J Simmons
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bci4iugw
materials: Move tissue to a 2ml tube containing ~1.8ml of chelation buffer and place on a tube rotator with continuous rotation. Labquake Rotisserie (Tube Rotator, Thermo Scientific, TS-4002110Q, https://s3.amazonaws.com/protocols-files/private/e561a1a3affcf1dddc10b95cf7c319b0cd9fc40d10ab824c30eebd12deacd7aa/by2i7w7e.jpg )

Hydrate, aliquot, and freeze 2x DNAse DNAse Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #DN25-100MG (CAS: 9003-98-9) DPBS without calcium & magnesium Corning Catalog #21-031-CV Hydrate to 5mg/ml in DPBS; keep cold; aliquot 1ml each into 2ml tubes and freeze immediately. Store at -20˚c and use within 6 months.

Hydrate, aliquot, and freeze 20x Cold protease Protease from Bacillus Licheniformis Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #P5380 Hydrate to 100mg/ml in molecular grade H2O; keep cold; aliquot 100ul each into 2ml tubes and freeze immediately. Store at -20˚c and use within 6 months.

steps.title: Record tissue metadata
steps.instruction: Upon receipt, inspect the biopsy, note Accession number, size (draw a spot describing shape – flat, round, etc.), appearance, and presence of blood; do not weigh the sample (typical size 20‑40 mg).

steps.title: Prepare chelation buffer
steps.instruction: Make chelation buffer using DPBS without Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ (Corning Catalog #21-031-CV) and EDTA 0.5 M pH 8 (Corning Catalog #46-034-CI).

steps.title: Prepare DTT aliquots
steps.instruction: Dilute 1 M DTT (Teknova Catalog #D9750) 1:9 with molecular‑grade H₂O to obtain 0.1 M DTT; mix well, aliquot 1–2 mL, freeze at –20 °C (up to 6 months) and use aliquots within 1 week of thawing.

steps.title: Prepare DNAse solution
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL DPBS to a frozen 1 mL aliquot of 2× DNAse, let thaw on the bench, then keep on ice until needed.

steps.title: Prepare dissociation solution
steps.instruction: Combine 1.9 mL 1× DNAse (from the thawed DNAse solution) with a frozen 100 µL aliquot of 20× cold Protease; mix by pipetting to give the final dissociation solution.

steps.title: Trim solid tissue
steps.instruction: If the biopsy is solid or pedunculated, bisect or trisect it to increase surface area, cutting no smaller than 2 mm pieces.

steps.title: Remove chelation buffer
steps.instruction: Gently remove the chelation buffer from the tube and resuspend the tissue in DPBS.

steps.title: Wash tissue in DPBS
steps.instruction: Wash the tissue gently with DPBS to remove debris and excess transport media.

steps.title: Filter tissue suspension
steps.instruction: Pipette the suspension to mix, then transfer onto a 70 µm mini‑strainer (pluriSelect Life Science Catalog #43-10070-50) placed in a clean tube on a cold rack; allow cells to filter by gravity and check the filtrate for cells before proceeding.

steps.title: Replace chelation buffer
steps.instruction: At 30 minutes and again at 1 hour into the chelation step, gently add fresh chelation buffer, leaving enough air in the tube to displace (agitate) the tissue during rotation.

steps.title: Add dissociation solution
steps.instruction: Remove DPBS from the tissue and resuspend the sample in 1.8 mL of the prepared dissociation solution, ensuring sufficient air remains in the tube for displacement on inversion.

steps.title: Incubate on rotator
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a continuous‑rotation rotator (Labquake Rotisserie, Thermo Scientific TS‑4002110Q) and rotate throughout the dissociation period.

steps.title: Trituration at 25 min
steps.instruction: At 25 minutes (end of dissociation) triturate the suspension 5–10 times with a standard P‑1000 tip, deforming tissue as it enters the tip to release cells into the supernatant; the supernatant should become cloudy. Examine on a hemocytometer: cells should be mostly single or in clusters ≤10, with ≥100 K cells total. If yield is low, incubate an additional 5 minutes and triturate again.

steps.title: Centrifuge cells
steps.instruction: Spin the suspension at 700 × g (700 rcf) for 5 minutes at 4–6 °C. Verify that a visible pellet has formed before removing the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant, then resuspend the cell pellet in DPBS using a wide‑bore P‑1000 tip. If the pellet does not form, increase the speed by ~100 × g. Note that dying cells may produce stringy aggregates that should remain in the supernatant and be removed during washes.

steps.title: Wash cells twice
steps.instruction: Repeat the DPBS wash (remove supernatant, add fresh DPBS, resuspend) two additional times, checking cell number and quality after each resuspension.

steps.title: Final resuspension and filtration
steps.instruction: On the third resuspension, gently resuspend cells in DPBS (or single‑cell running buffer) at roughly twice the desired final concentration or higher, then pass the suspension through a 70 µm Flowmi filter (Bel‑Art) into a clean tube.

steps.title: Assess and proceed
steps.instruction: Check cell concentration and viability, dilute as needed, and move the suspension to the encapsulation step.
